description: Makes a melody by sampling a free-running oscillator at each clock, so the notes step through a pattern that repeats; the clock cable's channel count sets how many voices play

params.text: Draws a new random oscillator frequency, between 440Hz and three octaves above it, which is a new melody; held down it keeps drawing another every sample
Sets the voltage the melody reaches at the far end of the oscillator cycle, -10V to +10V
Sets the voltage the melody starts from at the near end of the oscillator cycle, -10V to +10V

inputs.text: Samples a new note on each rise past 2V; each channel of the cable reads the oscillator a fixed fraction of a cycle from the last
Draws a new random oscillator frequency on each rise past 2V, which is a new melody
Replaces the Max knob while a cable is patched, a volt of range per volt
Replaces the Min knob while a cable is patched, a volt of range per volt

outputs.text: The melody, one channel per clock channel, each note held until the next clock

notes: nothing comes out until a clock is patched: the output takes its channel count from the clock cable, and with no cable there it has no channels at all
the two range knobs start with Max at -5V and Min at +5V, the opposite way round to their names, so a fresh module sweeps downward until one of them is moved
the melody is the oscillator's frequency and it is saved with the patch, so the same one comes back when the patch is loaded

inputs.1:
high above 2V · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
